text: Let me walk you through our revenue over the last five years. From 2020 to 2022, we saw a thirty percent year-over-year increase in revenue. In 2023, revenue plateaued, because two large clients changed their IT teams. The reduction in operating costs that year allowed us to stay profitable. Since then, the increase in our run rate shows that the trajectory is back. Our addressable market in Latin America is still largely untapped.

When a founder tells me we grew a lot, I hear nothing. I cannot check a lot. When he tells me we saw a thirty percent year-over-year increase in recurring revenue, I hear a number I can check in the data room. And when he says revenue plateaued in 2023, and explains why, I trust him more, not less. Every company has a bad year. What worries me is a founder who cannot describe it.

Before our sale, our advisor made me rewrite every slide. On the first version I wrote: we grew fast, and then we cut costs. She told me that sounded like a story about me. The new version said: a forty percent increase in revenue between 2019 and 2021, and a reduction in operating costs that allowed us to break even in a difficult year. Same numbers. But in the meeting, the buyer started asking about the future, not about the past.
We saw a twenty percent year-over-year increase in revenue.
Our growth trajectory has been stable for five years.
The reduction in costs allowed us to break even.
Our run rate is now ninety million reais a year.
The new unit broke even in its second year.
Revenue plateaued in 2023, and then it grew again.
We saw a thirty percent year-over-year increase in revenue.
Our addressable market is still largely untapped.
